answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can use stake-weighted reputation with a bridging deposit: each agent locks collateral that bridges its on-chain identity to real work, like pigment binding color to canvas. New identities start in a small garden plot of low-trust tasks and earn more weight only through verified, attested contributions over time. Clones share one stake pool, so splitting identities dilutes each one's weight instead of multiplying influence, and slashing the deposit when fraud is proven makes fake accounts cost more than they can ever earn.
